units.zh: 梁書卷第十二 列傳第六
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 12, Biographies 6
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 12, Biographies 6

units.zh: 柳惔 弟忱 席闡文 韋叡 族弟愛
units.en: Liu Tan; his younger brother Chen; Xi Chanwen; Wei Rui; and clan cousin Ai
units.literal: Liu Tan; younger brother Chen; Xi Chanwen; Wei Rui; clan cousin Ai

units.zh: 柳惔，字文通，河東解人也。
units.en: Liu Tan, styled Wentong, came from Jie in Hedong.
units.literal: Liu Tan, styled Wentong, was a native of Jie in Hedong.

units.zh: 父世隆，齊司空。
units.en: His father Shilong had been Qi's minister of works.
units.literal: His father Shilong was Minister of Works in Qi.

units.zh: 惔年十七，齊武帝爲中軍，命爲參軍，轉主簿。
units.en: At seventeen, with Emperor Wu of Qi as central army commander, Tan became his retainer, then chief clerk.
units.literal: At seventeen, when Emperor Wu of Qi was Central Army commander, Tan was appointed a retainer, then transferred to chief clerk.

units.zh: 齊初，入爲尚書三公郎，累遷太子中舍人，巴東王子響友。
units.en: Early in Qi he entered the secretariat as three-ducal attendant, rose to crown prince gentleman companion, and was made Friend of the Prince of Badong, Zi Xiang.
units.literal: Early in Qi he entered the Masters of Writing as attendant of the Three Ducal Officials, rose through posts to crown prince gentleman companion, and became Friend of the Prince of Badong, Zi Xiang.

units.zh: 子響爲荊州，惔隨之鎮。
units.en: When Zi Xiang went to Jing province, Tan followed him there.
units.literal: When Zi Xiang took Jing province, Tan followed him to the post.

units.zh: 子響昵近小人，惔知將爲禍，稱疾還京。
units.en: Zi Xiang clung to petty men; Tan foresaw ruin, claimed illness, and went back to the capital.
units.literal: Zi Xiang doted on petty men; Tan saw disaster coming, feigned illness, and returned to the capital.

units.zh: 及難作，惔以先歸得免。
units.en: When trouble came, Tan escaped because he had returned first.
units.literal: When the crisis broke, Tan was spared because he had left early.

units.zh: 歷中書侍郎，中護軍長史。
units.en: He was gentleman of the secretariat and long-term staff officer to the central guard.
units.literal: He served as gentleman of the Secretariat and long-term staff officer to the Central Guard.

units.zh: 出爲新安太守，居郡，以無政績，免歸。
units.en: He went out as Xin'an prefect, achieved nothing in office, and was sent home.
units.literal: He went out as prefect of Xin'an; in the commandery he achieved nothing and was dismissed.

units.zh: 久之，爲右軍諮議參軍事。
units.en: Long afterward he became an advisory staff officer of the right army.
units.literal: After a long interval he became advisory staff officer to the Right Army.

units.zh: 建武末，爲西戎校尉、梁南秦二州刺史。
units.en: At the end of Jianwu he was western rong colonel and inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
units.literal: At the end of Jianwu he was made Colonel of the Western Rong and inspector of Liang and Southern Qin provinces.

units.zh: 及高祖起兵，惔舉漢中應義。
units.en: When Gaozu rose in arms, Tan raised Hanzhong for the cause.
units.literal: When Gaozu raised the army, Tan raised Hanzhong in support of the righteous cause.

units.zh: 和帝卽位，以爲侍中，領前軍將軍。
units.en: Emperor He made him attendant within and acting front army general.
units.literal: When Emperor He took the throne, Tan was made Attendant Within and given acting charge as Front Army General.

units.zh: 高祖踐阼，徵爲護軍將軍，未拜，仍遷太子詹事，加散騎常侍。
units.en: Gaozu summoned him as protector of the army; before he took the post he became heir apparent household head and scattered cavalry attendant.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Tan was summoned as Protector of the Army General; before he accepted he was transferred to Household Head of the Heir Apparent with additional appointment as Scattered Cavalry Attendant.

units.zh: 論功封曲江縣侯，邑千戶。
units.en: For merit he was made marquis of Qujiang with one thousand households.
units.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang with a fief of one thousand households.

units.zh: 高祖因讌爲詩以貽惔曰：「爾實冠羣后，惟餘實念功。」
units.en: At a feast Gaozu wrote a poem for Tan: "You alone crown the lords; only you keep my deeds in mind."
units.literal: At a banquet Gaozu composed a poem and gave it to Tan, saying: "You truly crown the feudal lords; only you truly remember my merit."

units.zh: 又嘗侍座，高祖曰：「徐元瑜違命嶺南，《周書》罪不相及，朕已宥其諸子，何如？」
units.en: Another time at court Gaozu said, "Xu Yuanyu rebelled in Lingnan. The Book of Zhou says punishment does not chain to kin—I have pardoned his sons. What say you?"
units.literal: On another occasion, while attending him, Gaozu said: "Xu Yuanyu defied orders in Lingnan—the Book of Zhou says crimes do not reach kin. I have already pardoned his sons. What do you think?"

units.zh: 惔對曰：「罰不及嗣，賞延于世，今復見之聖朝。」
units.en: Tan answered, "Punishment stops at the man; reward flows to his line—we see that again in this sage reign."
units.literal: Tan replied: "Punishment does not reach heirs; reward extends through generations—today we see it again in the sage court."

units.zh: 時以爲知言。
units.en: Men called it words that knew the times.
units.literal: The age regarded it as perceptive speech.

units.zh: 尋遷尚書右僕射。
units.en: He was soon made right vice director of the masters of writing.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 天監四年，大舉北伐，臨川王宏都督衆軍，以惔爲副。
units.en: In Tianjian year four the court launched a great northern campaign; the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, commanded the armies with Tan as deputy.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian a great northern campaign was launched; the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, commanded the massed armies, with Tan as his deputy.

units.zh: 軍還，復爲僕射。
units.en: When the armies came home he was again vice director.
units.literal: When the army returned, he again became vice director.

units.zh: 以久疾，轉金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，給親信二十人。
units.en: Long illness moved him to golden crown and purple light grandee, scattered cavalry attendant, and twenty trusted retainers.
units.literal: Because of long illness he was transferred to Golden Crown and Purple Light Grandee with additional appointment as Scattered Cavalry Attendant and twenty trusted retainers.

units.zh: 未拜，出爲使持節、安南將軍、湘州刺史。
units.en: Before he took office he went out with credentials as pacify-the-south general and Xiangzhou inspector.
units.literal: Before he accepted the post he went out as envoy with credentials, Pacify the South General, and inspector of Xiang province.

units.zh: 六年十月，卒于州，時年四十六。
units.en: In the tenth month of year six he died in the province at forty-six.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year he died in the province, aged forty-six.

units.zh: 高祖爲素服舉哀。
units.en: Gaozu wore undyed robes and mourned him.
units.literal: Gaozu wore plain robes and raised lament for him.

units.zh: 贈侍中、撫軍將軍，給鼓吹一部。
units.en: Posthumously he was attendant within and pacify-the-army general, with one suite of drums and pipes.
units.literal: He was posthumously granted Attendant Within and Pacify the Army General, with one suite of drums and pipes.

units.zh: 諡曰穆。
units.en: Posthumous name Mu.
units.literal: Posthumous name: Mu.

units.zh: 惔著《仁政傳》及諸詩賦，粗有辭義。
units.en: Tan wrote Record of Benevolent Government and poems and fu with modest literary force.
units.literal: Tan wrote the Record of Benevolent Government and various poems and rhapsodies, all with some literary merit.

units.zh: 子照嗣。
units.en: His son Zhao inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Zhao succeeded him.

units.zh: 惔第四弟憕，亦有美譽，歷侍中、鎮西長史。
units.en: Tan's fourth brother Cheng was also praised; he was attendant within and pacify-the-west long-term staff officer.
units.literal: Tan's fourth younger brother Cheng also enjoyed a fine reputation; he served as Attendant Within and long-term staff officer to Pacify the West.

units.zh: 天監十二年，卒，贈寧遠將軍、豫州刺史。
units.en: In Tianjian year twelve he died and was posthumously pacify-the-distant general and Yuzhou inspector.
units.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianjian he died; posthumously he was granted Pacify the Distant General and inspector of Yu province.

units.zh: 忱字文若，惔第五弟也。
units.en: Chen, styled Wenruo, was Tan's fifth brother.
units.literal: Chen, styled Wenruo, was Tan's fifth younger brother.

units.zh: 年數歲，父世隆及母閻氏時寢疾，忱不解帶經年。
units.en: Still a child, he tended his father Shilong and mother Lady Yan through long illness without undoing his belt for a year.
units.literal: When he was only a few years old, his father Shilong and his mother, Lady Yan, lay ill; Chen went without loosening his belt for a full year.

units.zh: 及居喪，以毀聞。
units.en: In mourning his grief was famed for wrecking his body.
units.literal: In mourning he was famed for destroying his health.

units.zh: 起家爲司徒行參軍，累遷太子中舍人，西中郎主簿，功曹史。
units.en: He began on the minister of education's staff, rose to crown prince gentleman companion, western Zhonglang chief clerk, and merit-records officer.
units.literal: He first entered office as a retainer on the Minister of Education's staff, rose through posts to crown prince gentleman companion, Western Zhonglang chief clerk, and merit-records officer.

units.zh: 齊東昏遣巴西太守劉山陽由荊襲高祖，西中郎長史蕭穎胄計未有定，召忱及其所親席闡文等夜入議之。
units.en: Dong Hun sent Brazil prefect Liu Shanyang from Jing against Gaozu; Xiao Yingzhou, western Zhonglang long-term staff officer, had no plan yet and called Chen, Xi Chanwen, and others to a night council.
units.literal: Dong Hun sent Liu Shanyang, prefect of Brazil, from Jing to strike Gaozu; the Western Zhonglang long-term staff officer Xiao Yingzhou had not settled on a plan and summoned Chen and his intimate Xi Chanwen and others to enter by night to discuss it.

units.zh: 忱曰：「朝廷狂悖，爲惡日滋。
units.en: Chen said, "The court is deranged and wicked, and its crimes swell daily.
units.literal: Chen said: "The court is mad and wicked; its evils grow day by day.

units.zh: 頃聞京師長者，莫不重足累息；
units.en: Lately I hear that in the capital the old and honored dare not breathe aloud;
units.literal: Of late I hear that elders in the capital—none do not walk on tiptoe, holding their breath;

units.zh: 今幸在遠，得假日自安。
units.en: we are lucky to be distant and may steal a day's peace.
units.literal: we are fortunate to be far away and may take a day to rest in safety.

units.zh: 雍州之事，且藉以相斃耳。
units.en: As for Yongzhou, for now let it kill them for us.
units.literal: The Yongzhou affair—let us for now rely on it to destroy one another.

units.zh: 獨不見蕭令君乎？
units.en: Have you not seen Commander Xiao?
units.literal: Have you alone not seen Commander Xiao?

units.zh: 以精兵數千，破崔氏十萬衆，竟爲羣邪所陷，禍酷相尋。
units.en: A few thousand elite troops broke Cui's hundred thousand, yet villains trapped him and ruin followed ruin.
units.literal: With a few thousand crack troops he shattered Cui's force of a hundred thousand, yet in the end was trapped by a pack of villains, calamity heaped upon calamity.

units.zh: 前事之不忘，後事之師也。
units.en: What came before, if remembered, teaches what comes after.
units.literal: What is past and not forgotten is the teacher of what follows.

units.zh: 若使彼凶心已逞，豈知使君不系踵而及？
units.en: If their evil will is satisfied, do you think our lord will not be chained next?
units.literal: If their wicked hearts have already had their way, do you suppose our lord will not be next in chains?

units.zh: 且雍州士銳糧多，蕭使君雄姿冠世，必非山陽所能擬；
units.en: Yongzhou has sharp troops and full granaries; Commander Xiao's heroism tops the age—Liu Shanyang cannot compare;
units.literal: Moreover Yongzhou's soldiers are sharp and its grain abundant; Commander Xiao's heroic bearing crowns the age—he is surely not someone Liu Shanyang can match;

units.zh: 若破山陽，荊州復受失律之責。
units.en: break Liu Shanyang and Jingzhou again pays for failure in arms.
units.literal: if you defeat Liu Shanyang, Jingzhou will again bear blame for losing discipline.

units.zh: 進退無可，且深慮之。」
units.en: Advance or retreat, there is no road—think hard on this."
units.literal: Whether you advance or retreat there is no way—ponder this deeply."

units.zh: 闡文亦深勸同高祖。
units.en: Xi Chanwen too pressed hard for alliance with Gaozu.
units.literal: Xi Chanwen also urged joining Gaozu in depth.

units.zh: 穎胄乃誘斬山陽，以忱爲寧朔將軍。
units.en: Yingzhou baited and killed Shanyang and made Chen pacify-the-north general.
units.literal: Yingzhou then lured and killed Shanyang and made Chen Pacify the North General.

units.zh: 和帝卽位，爲尚書吏部郎，進號輔國將軍、南平太守。
units.en: Emperor He made him personnel gentleman of the masters of writing, then supporting state general and Nanping prefect.
units.literal: When Emperor He took the throne, Chen was made Gentleman of the Masters of Writing in the Ministry of Personnel and advanced in rank to Supporting State General and prefect of Nanping.

units.zh: 尋遷侍中、冠軍將軍，太守如故。
units.en: Soon he was attendant within and champion general, still holding the prefecture.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Attendant Within and Champion General, retaining the prefecture.

units.zh: 轉吏部尚書，不拜。
units.en: He was offered minister of the masters of writing and declined.
units.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Masters of Writing but did not accept.

units.zh: 郢州平，穎胄議遷都夏口，忱復固諫，以爲巴硤未賓，不宜輕舍根本，搖動民志。
units.en: When Yingzhou was pacified, Yingzhou debated moving the capital to Xiakou; Chen again remonstrated firmly that Ba and the Gorges were not yet subdued and one should not lightly abandon the root and shake the people's hearts.
units.literal: When Ying city was pacified, Yingzhou debated moving the capital to Xiakou; Chen again remonstrated firmly, holding that Ba and the Gorges were not yet subdued and one should not lightly abandon the root and shake the people's hearts.

units.zh: 穎胄不從。
units.en: Yingzhou would not listen.
units.literal: Yingzhou did not heed him.

units.zh: 俄而巴東兵至硤口，遷都之議乃息。
units.en: Soon Ba-Dong troops reached the gorge and the move was dropped.
units.literal: Before long Ba-Dong troops reached the gorge mouth and talk of moving the capital ceased.

units.zh: 論者以爲見機。
units.en: Men said he had read the times.
units.literal: Commentators held that he had seen the moment.

units.zh: 高祖踐阼，以忱爲五兵尚書，領驍騎將軍。
units.en: Gaozu made him minister of the five armies and acting valiant cavalry general.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Chen was made Minister of the Five Armies and given acting charge as Valiant Cavalry General.

units.zh: 論建義功，封州陵伯，邑七百戶。
units.en: For founding merit he was baron of Zhouling with seven hundred households.
units.literal: For merit in founding the righteous cause he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling with a fief of seven hundred households.

units.zh: 天監二年，出爲安西長史、冠軍將軍、南郡太守。
units.en: In Tianjian year two he was pacify-the-west long-term staff officer, champion general, and Nan commandery prefect.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he went out as long-term staff officer to Pacify the West, Champion General, and prefect of Nan commandery.

units.zh: 六年，徵爲員外散騎常侍、太子右衛率。
units.en: In year six he was summoned as extraordinary scattered-cavalry attendant and heir apparent right guard commandant.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Extraordinary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

units.zh: 未發，遷持節、督湘州諸軍事、輔國將軍、湘州刺史。
units.en: Before he left he became credentialed envoy, Xiang military supervisor, supporting state general, and Xiangzhou inspector.
units.literal: Before he set out he was transferred to envoy with credentials, supervisor of military affairs in Xiang province, Supporting State General, and inspector of Xiang province.

units.zh: 八年，坐輒放從軍丁免。
units.en: In year eight he was removed for freeing conscripts without leave.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was dismissed for releasing conscript soldiers on his own authority.

units.zh: 俄入爲秘書監，遷散騎常侍，轉祠部尚書，未拜遇疾，詔改授給事中、光祿大夫，疾篤不拜。
units.en: Soon he was secretariat director, then scattered-cavalry attendant, then minister of sacrifices; illness came before he took office and an edict made him palace supervisor and splendid-light grandee, but he was too ill to accept.
units.literal: Soon he entered the court as Director of the Secretariat, was transferred to Scattered Cavalry Attendant, then Minister of Sacrifices—but before he accepted he fell ill; an edict changed his appointment to Supervisor of the Palace and Grandee of Splendid Light; his illness was severe and he did not accept.

units.zh: 十年，卒於家，時年四十一。
units.en: In year ten he died at home at forty-one.
units.literal: In the tenth year he died at home, aged forty-one.

units.zh: 追贈中書令，諡曰穆。
units.en: Posthumously he was director of the secretariat; posthumous name Mu.
units.literal: Posthumously he was granted Director of the Secretariat; posthumous name: Mu.

units.zh: 子範嗣。
units.en: His son Fan inherited the line.
units.literal: His son Fan succeeded him.

units.zh: 席闡文，安定臨涇人也。
units.en: Xi Chanwen came from Linjing in Anding.
units.literal: Xi Chanwen was a native of Linjing in Anding.

units.zh: 少孤貧，涉獵書史。
units.en: Orphaned and poor in youth, he read widely in books and histories.
units.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he ranged widely through books and histories.

units.zh: 齊初，爲雍州刺史蕭赤斧中兵參軍，由是與其子穎胄善。
units.en: Early in Qi he was central army retainer to Yongzhou inspector Xiao Chifu and grew close to his son Yingzhou.
units.literal: Early in Qi he was a central army retainer to Xiao Chifu, inspector of Yong province, and through this became close to Chifu's son Yingzhou.

units.zh: 復歷西中郎中兵參軍，領城局。
units.en: He later was western Zhonglang central army retainer and held the city bureau.
units.literal: He later served as central army retainer in the Western Zhonglang headquarters and held charge of the city bureau.

units.zh: 高祖之將起義也，闡文深勸之，穎胄同焉，仍遣田祖恭私報高祖，并獻銀裝刀，高祖報以金如意。
units.en: As Gaozu prepared to rise, Chanwen urged him hard; Yingzhou agreed and sent Tian Zugong secretly to Gaozu with a silver-mounted knife—Gaozu answered with a gold ruyi.
units.literal: When Gaozu was about to raise the righteous army, Chanwen urged him deeply; Yingzhou agreed and sent Tian Zugong in secret to report to Gaozu, also presenting a silver-mounted knife—Gaozu replied with a gold ruyi scepter.

units.zh: 和帝稱尊號，爲給事黃門侍郎，尋遷衛尉卿。
units.en: When Emperor He took the throne Chanwen was yellow-gates attendant, then court commandant.
units.literal: When Emperor He assumed the exalted title, Chanwen was made Attendant of the Yellow Gates in the Secretariat and soon transferred to Commandant of the Court.

units.zh: 穎胄暴卒，州府騷擾，闡文以和帝幼弱，中流任重，時始興王憺留鎮雍部，用與西朝羣臣迎王總州事，故賴以寧輯。
units.en: Yingzhou died suddenly and the province shook; Chanwen said the emperor was young and the midstream heavy—Prince of Shixing Dan held Yong, and Chanwen with western ministers brought him to head the province and calm the land.
units.literal: When Yingzhou died suddenly, the province and prefecture were in turmoil; Chanwen held that Emperor He was young and weak while the midstream bore heavy responsibility—at the time the Prince of Shixing, Dan, was left to guard Yong, and Chanwen joined the western court ministers in welcoming the prince to take overall charge of the province, and through this order was restored.

units.zh: 高祖受禪，除都官尚書、輔國將軍。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne Chanwen was minister of punishments and supporting state general.
units.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Chanwen was made Minister of Punishments and Supporting State General.

units.zh: 封山陽伯，邑七百戶。
units.en: He was baron of Shanyang with seven hundred households.
units.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Shanyang with a fief of seven hundred households.

units.zh: 出爲東陽太守，又改封湘西，戶邑如故。
units.en: He went out as Dongyang prefect, then was re-enfeoffed as baron of Xiangxi with the same fief.
units.literal: He went out as prefect of Dongyang and was later re-enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangxi, his household fief unchanged.

units.zh: 視事二年，以清白著稱，卒於官。
units.en: In two years in office his integrity was famed; he died there.
units.literal: In two years of office he was famed for integrity and died in his post.

units.zh: 詔賻錢三萬，布五十匹。
units.en: An edict granted thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth.
units.literal: An edict granted thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth for his funeral.

units.zh: 諡曰威。
units.en: Posthumous name Wei.
units.literal: Posthumous name: Wei.

units.zh: 韋叡，字懷文，京兆杜陵人也。
units.en: Wei Rui, styled Huaiwen, came from Duling in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Wei Rui, styled Huaiwen, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 自漢丞相賢以後，世爲三輔著姓。
units.en: Since Han chancellor Xian, for generations the clan was a great house of the three metropolises.
units.literal: From Chancellor Xian of Han onward, for generations his clan was a leading surname of the Three Metropolises.

units.zh: 祖玄，避吏隱於長安南山。
units.en: His grandfather Xuan hid on Chang'an's southern hills to avoid office.
units.literal: His grandfather Xuan, to avoid summons as an official, hid on the southern slopes of Chang'an.

units.zh: 宋武帝入關，以太尉掾徵，不至。
units.en: Song's Emperor Wu entering the passes summoned him as grand commandant aide; he did not go.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song entered the passes, he was summoned as aide to the Grand Commandant but did not come.

units.zh: 伯父祖征，宋末爲光祿勳。
units.en: His uncle Zuzheng, late in Song, was chamberlain for attendants.
units.literal: His father's elder brother Zuzheng, at the end of Song, was Chamberlain for Attendants.

units.zh: 父祖歸，寧遠長史。
units.en: His father Zugui was pacify-the-distant long-term staff officer.
units.literal: His father Zugui was long-term staff officer to Pacify the Distant.

units.zh: 叡事繼母以孝聞。
units.en: Rui was famed for filial service to his stepmother.
units.literal: Rui served his stepmother with a fame for filial piety.

units.zh: 叡兄纂、闡，並早知名。
units.en: His elder brothers Zuan and Chan were known early as well.
units.literal: Rui's elder brothers Zuan and Chan were both known early.

units.zh: 纂、叡皆好學，闡有清操。
units.en: Zuan and Rui loved study; Chan had clear integrity.
units.literal: Zuan and Rui both loved learning; Chan had pure conduct.

units.zh: 祖征累爲郡守，每攜叡之職，視之如子。
units.en: Zuzheng held many prefectures and always took Rui along, treating him like a son.
units.literal: Zuzheng repeatedly served as prefect and always took Rui to his post, treating him as a son.

units.zh: 時叡內兄王憕、姨弟杜惲，並有鄉里盛名。
units.en: Then his brother-in-law Wang Cheng and cousin Du Yun were famed in the district.
units.literal: At the time Rui's brother-in-law Wang Cheng and cousin Du Yun both enjoyed great local fame.

units.zh: 祖征謂叡曰：「汝自謂何如憕、惲？」
units.en: Zuzheng asked Rui, "How do you think you compare to Cheng and Yun?"
units.literal: Zuzheng said to Rui: "How do you rate yourself beside Cheng and Yun?"

units.zh: 叡謙不敢對。
units.en: Rui modestly would not answer.
units.literal: Rui modestly did not answer.

units.zh: 祖征曰：「汝文章或小減，學識當過之；
units.en: Zuzheng said, "Your writing may fall a little short, but your learning should exceed theirs;
units.literal: Zuzheng said: "Your literary writing may be somewhat less, but your learning should surpass theirs;

units.zh: 然而幹國家，成功業，皆莫汝逮也。」
units.en: yet in serving the state and winning great deeds, none can match you."
units.literal: yet in managing the state and accomplishing great works, none of them can match you."

units.zh: 外兄杜幼文爲梁州刺史，要叡俱行。
units.en: Cousin Du Youwen was Liangzhou inspector and asked Rui to accompany him.
units.literal: His cousin Du Youwen was inspector of Liang province and asked Rui to go with him.

units.zh: 梁土富饒，往者多以賄敗；
units.en: Liang was rich; many who went there were ruined by bribes;
units.literal: Liang territory was rich; those who went there often fell to bribery;

units.zh: 叡時雖幼，獨用廉聞。
units.en: yet Rui, though young, alone was famed for integrity.
units.literal: though Rui was still young, he alone was famed for integrity.

units.zh: 宋永光初，袁顗爲雍州刺史，見而異之，引爲主簿。
units.en: In Song's first Yongguang year Yuan Yan was Inspector of Yongzhou; he saw Rui, marveled, and made him chief clerk.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongguang of Song, Yuan Yan was Inspector of Yongzhou; he saw Rui and was struck with wonder, and took him as chief clerk.

units.zh: 顗到州，與鄧琬起兵，叡求出爲義成郡，故免顗之禍。
units.en: Yan reached his post and rose with Deng Wan; Rui secured an exit as administrator of Yicheng and missed Yan's downfall.
units.literal: When Yan reached his province he joined Deng Wan in raising troops; Rui asked to go out as Administrator of Yicheng and so escaped the ruin that overtook Yan.

units.zh: 後爲晉平王左常侍，遷司空桂陽王行參軍，隨齊司空柳世隆守郢城，拒荊州刺史沈攸之。
units.en: He became regular attendant to the Prince of Jinping, then staff officer to the Prince of Guiyang under the Minister of Works, and followed Liu Shilong in the defense of Yingcheng against Shen Youzhi.
units.literal: Later he was Regular Attendant to the Prince of Jinping, then a staff officer on the Prince of Guiyang's suite under the Minister of Works; he followed Qi Minister of Works Liu Shilong in holding Yingcheng against Jingzhou Inspector Shen Youzhi.

units.zh: 攸之平，遷前軍中兵參軍。
units.en: After Youzhi's defeat he was made army aide of the van.
units.literal: When Youzhi was pacified, he was promoted to Army Aide of the Van.

units.zh: 久之，爲廣德令。
units.en: In time he became magistrate of Guangde.
units.literal: After some time he was made magistrate of Guangde.

units.zh: 累遷齊興太守、本州別駕、長水校尉、右軍將軍。
units.en: He advanced through administrator of Qixing, provincial aide, colonel of the Long River, and general of the right.
units.literal: He rose repeatedly to Administrator of Qixing, provincial aide of his native prefecture, Colonel of the Long River, and General of the Right.

units.zh: 齊末多故，不欲遠鄉里，求爲上庸太守，加建威將軍。
units.en: Qi's last days were full of upheaval; he did not wish to leave his native hills and asked for Shangyong, with the added title general who establishes might.
units.literal: At the end of Qi turmoil was everywhere; unwilling to leave his home country, he asked to be Administrator of Shangyong, with the additional rank General Who Establishes Might.

units.zh: 俄而太尉陳顯達、護軍將軍崔慧景頻逼京師，民心遑駭，未有所定，西土人謀之於叡。
units.en: Soon Chen Xianda and Cui Huijing harried the capital repeatedly; fear ran wild and the west turned to Rui for a plan.
units.literal: Before long Grand Marshal Chen Xianda and Protector of the Army Cui Huijing pressed the capital again and again; the people's hearts were frantic and nothing was settled, and the men of the western lands looked to Rui for counsel.

units.zh: 叡曰：「陳雖舊將，非命世才；
units.en: Rui said, "Chen is a veteran, yet not a man born for the times;
units.literal: Rui said, "Chen is an old commander, but no man of the age;

units.zh: 崔頗更事，懦而不武。
units.en: Cui has weathered many storms, yet he is soft and no soldier.
units.literal: Cui has seen much, but he is timid and no warrior.

units.zh: 其取赤族也，宜哉！
units.en: They deserve the extinction of their houses—of course they do!
units.literal: That their clans should be wiped to the last man is only fitting!

units.zh: 天下真人，殆興於吾州矣。」
units.en: The man Heaven favors will probably rise from our province."
units.literal: The true lord of the realm will likely rise from our province."

units.zh: 乃遣其二子，自結於高祖。
units.en: With that he sent his two sons to bind themselves to Gaozu.
units.literal: He then sent his two sons to attach themselves to Gaozu.

units.zh: 義兵檄至，叡率郡人伐竹爲筏，倍道來赴，有衆二千，馬二百匹。
units.en: The call to arms came; Rui had his district cut bamboo rafts, marched night and day, and arrived with two thousand foot and two hundred horse.
units.literal: When the righteous army's manifesto arrived, Rui led the people of his command to cut bamboo for rafts, came by forced marches, and brought two thousand men and two hundred horses.

units.zh: 高祖見叡甚悅，拊几曰：「他日見君之面，今日見君之心，吾事就矣。」
units.en: Gaozu rejoiced at the sight of him and smote the table: "I might have met your face another day; today I meet your heart—my work is done."
units.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased when he saw Rui and struck the table, saying, "Another day I would have seen your face; today I see your heart—my cause is assured."

units.zh: 義師克郢、魯，平加湖，叡多建謀策，皆見納用。
units.en: The righteous army took Ying and Lu and pacified Jiahu; Rui's counsel was offered at every turn and taken.
units.literal: The righteous army took Ying and Lu, pacified Jiahu Lake, and Rui offered many plans, all of which were adopted.

units.zh: 大軍發郢，謀留守將，高祖難其人；
units.en: The host marched from Ying and debated a garrison commander; Gaozu could find no fit man.
units.literal: When the great army set out from Ying, they debated who should stay to guard it; Gaozu found no man equal to the task.

units.zh: 久之，顧叡曰：「棄騏驥而不乘，焉遑遑而更索？」
units.en: At length he looked at Rui and said, "To abandon a stallion and go begging for another mount—what sort of hurry is that?"
units.literal: After a long while he turned to Rui and said, "To leave a thoroughbred unmounted and go running about for another—what folly is that?"

units.zh: 卽日以爲冠軍將軍、江夏太守，行郢府事。
units.en: That day he was made general of the champions, administrator of Jiangxia, and acting head of the Ying prefecture.
units.literal: That same day he was made General of the Champions, Administrator of Jiangxia, and acting governor of the Ying prefecture.

units.zh: 初，郢城之拒守也，男女口垂十萬，閉壘經年，疾疫死者十七八，皆積屍於床下，而生者寢處其上，每屋輒盈滿。
units.en: When Ying had been besieged, nearly a hundred thousand people were trapped inside for a year; plague killed seven or eight in ten—they piled the dead beneath the beds and slept above, house after house packed to the rafters.
units.literal: Earlier, when Ying city had held out under siege, the population within the walls had neared a hundred thousand; the gates were shut for a year, and of plague and sickness seven or eight in ten died—corpses were heaped under the beds while the living slept above them, and every house was packed full.

units.zh: 叡料簡隱恤，咸爲營理，於是死者得埋藏，生者反居業，百姓賴之。
units.en: Rui sorted the neglected and the suffering and set everything right; the dead were buried, the living went back to their work, and the people lived by his hand.
units.literal: Rui sifted the hidden cases and showed compassion; he had all of it put in order, so the dead were buried and the living returned to their trades—the people relied on him.

units.zh: 梁臺建，徵爲大理。
units.en: When the Liang platform rose he was called to be grand judge.
units.literal: When the Liang regime was established he was summoned as Grand Judge.

units.zh: 高祖卽位，遷廷尉，封都梁子，邑三百戶。
units.en: At Gaozu's accession he became minister of justice, enfeoffed viscount of Duliang with three hundred households.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Rui was made Minister of Justice and enfeoffed as Viscount of Duliang with a fief of three hundred households.

units.zh: 天監二年，改封永昌，戶邑如先。
units.en: In Tianjian year 2 he was re-enfeoffed as Yongchang, fief and households unchanged.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianjian his enfeoffment was changed to Yongchang, the households and fief as before.

units.zh: 東宮建，遷太子右衛率，出爲輔國將軍、豫州刺史、領歷陽太守。
units.en: The eastern palace rose; he became right commandant of the crown prince's guard, then went out as general who assists the state, inspector of Yuzhou, and administrator of Liyang.
units.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established he was made Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, then went out as General Who Assists the State, Inspector of Yuzhou, and concurrent Administrator of Liyang.

units.zh: 三年，魏遣衆來寇，率州兵擊走之。
units.en: In year 3 Wei raided; he led the province's soldiers and beat them back.
units.literal: In the third year Wei sent armies to raid; he led the provincial troops and drove them off.

units.zh: 四年，王師北伐，詔叡都督衆軍。
units.en: In year 4 the court marched north; Rui was ordered to command the armies.
units.literal: In the fourth year the imperial army marched north; an edict made Rui commander-in-chief of the massed forces.

units.zh: 叡遣長史王超宗、梁郡太守馮道根攻魏小峴城，未能拔。
units.en: He sent chief clerk Wang Chaozong and Liangjun administrator Feng Daogen against Xiaokeng; they failed to crack the walls.
units.literal: Rui sent Chief Clerk Wang Chaozong and Administrator of Liangjun Feng Daogen to attack the Wei fort of Xiaokeng, but they could not take it.

units.zh: 叡巡行圍柵，魏城中忽出數百人陳於門外，叡欲擊之，諸將皆曰：「向本輕來，未有戰備，徐還授甲，乃可進耳。」
units.en: Rui toured the encirclement; hundreds of Wei soldiers burst from the gate and drew up outside. He meant to hit them, but his officers said, "We came lightly, without armor—fall back, arm, then fight."
units.literal: Rui walked the siege lines; several hundred men suddenly sallied from the Wei city and formed ranks outside the gate. Rui meant to strike them, but the generals all said, "We came light, without battle gear—withdraw, arm, and then advance."

units.zh: 叡曰：「不然。
units.en: Rui said, "No.
units.literal: Rui said, "Not so.

units.zh: 魏城中二千餘人，閉門堅守，足以自保，無故出人於外，必其驍勇者也，若能挫之，其城自拔。」
units.en: Two thousand-odd men behind barred gates can hold that place. If they come out without reason, these are their bravest; crush them and the city will take itself."
units.literal: Within the Wei city are a little more than two thousand men, shut in behind closed gates—enough to hold themselves. For them to come out without cause means these must be their fiercest fighters; if we break them, the city will fall of itself.

units.zh: 衆猶遲疑，叡指其節曰；
units.en: The army still hung back; Rui pointed to his command baton and said:
units.literal: The host still hesitated; Rui pointed to his staff of command and said:

units.zh: 「朝廷授此，非以爲飾，韋叡之法，不可犯也。」
units.en: "The throne gave me this, not for show. Wei Rui's law is not to be broken."
units.literal: "The court gave this—not for ornament. Wei Rui's law admits no breach."

units.zh: 乃進兵。
units.en: He marched.
units.literal: He advanced.

units.zh: 士皆殊死戰，魏軍果敗走，因急攻之，中宿而城拔。
units.en: The soldiers fought to the death; Wei broke and ran, and he pressed hard—before midnight the walls were his.
units.literal: The men fought as if each meant to die; the Wei army broke and fled, and he pressed the assault—by midnight the city was his.

units.zh: 遂進討合肥。
units.en: Then he moved against Hefei.
units.literal: He then marched to invest Hefei.

units.zh: 先是，右軍司馬胡略等至合肥，久未能下，叡按行山川，曰：「吾聞『汾水可以灌平陽，絳水可以灌安邑』，卽此是也。」
units.en: Hu Lue and the rest had besieged Hefei without success. Rui walked the ground and said, "They say 'the Fen flooded Pingyang and the Jiang flooded Anyi'—here is the same trick."
units.literal: Earlier, Right Army Major Hu Lue and others had reached Hefei but long could not reduce it. Rui surveyed the rivers and hills and said, "I have heard that the Fen can flood Pingyang and the Jiang can flood Anyi—this is that same thing."

units.zh: 乃堰肥水，親自表率，頃之，堰成水通，舟艦繼至。
units.en: He dammed the Fei and led the work in person; soon the water flowed, and warships followed one after another.
units.literal: He dammed the Fei River and worked at the head of the labor himself; before long the dam was done, the water ran through, and war-boats came up in succession.

units.zh: 魏初分築東西小城夾合肥，叡先攻二城。
units.en: Wei had split Hefei with twin forts east and west; Rui struck those first.
units.literal: Wei had first built eastern and western forts flanking Hefei; Rui attacked the two cities first.

units.zh: 旣而魏援將揚靈胤帥軍五萬奄至，衆懼不敵，請表益兵。
units.en: Then Yang Lingyin came with fifty thousand in relief; fear spread, and they asked to petition for more troops.
units.literal: Then Wei's relief commander Yang Lingyin led fifty thousand men in a sudden arrival; the army feared it could not match them and asked to memorialize for reinforcements.

units.zh: 叡笑曰：「賊已至城下，方復求軍，臨難鑄兵，豈及馬腹？
units.en: Rui laughed: "The foe is at the wall and you want more men—to cast weapons mid-battle, will that reach the horse's belly?
units.literal: Rui laughed and said, "The enemy is already at the walls and you ask for soldiers—who forges blades when the battle is on? Will that reach the horse's belly in time?

units.zh: 且吾求濟師，彼亦徵衆，猶如吳益巴丘，蜀增白帝耳。
units.en: If we beg for reinforcements, they will summon theirs too—Wu thickening Baqiu while Shu thickened White Emperor.
units.literal: If we ask for help, they too will summon hosts—like Wu reinforcing Baqiu while Shu reinforced White Emperor.

units.zh: 『師克在和不在衆』，古之義也。」
units.en: 'The army wins by unity, not by mass'—so the ancients taught."
units.literal: 'Victory lies in harmony, not in numbers'—that is the ancient teaching."

units.zh: 因與戰，破之，軍人少安。
units.en: He fought and routed them; the men drew breath again.
units.literal: He gave battle and broke them; the army breathed a little easier.

units.zh: 初，肥水堰立，使軍主王懷靜築城於岸守之，魏攻陷懷靜城，千餘人皆沒。
units.en: When the dam went up he left Wang Huaijing to fortify the bank; Wei stormed that fort and a thousand men were lost.
units.literal: When the Fei dam was first raised, he had Army Commander Wang Huaijing build a fort on the bank to hold it; Wei attacked and took Huaijing's fort, and more than a thousand men perished.

units.zh: 魏人乘勝至叡堤下，其勢甚盛，軍監潘靈祐勸叡退還巢湖，諸將又請走保三叉。
units.en: Wei surged to the dike in strength; Pan Lingyou urged retreat to Chaohu, and the officers again begged to fall back to Sancha.
units.literal: The Wei men pressed their victory to Rui's embankment in great force; Army Supervisor Pan Lingyou urged Rui to fall back to Chaohu Lake, and the generals again asked to retreat to Sancha.

units.zh: 叡怒曰：「寧有此邪！
units.en: Rui raged, "How could there be such a thing!
units.literal: Rui said in anger, "Could there be such a thing!

units.zh: 將軍死綏，有前無却。」
units.en: A general dies with his banner—forward only, never back."
units.literal: A general dies with his colors—there is advance, no retreat."

units.zh: 因令取傘扇麾幢，樹之堤下，示無動志。
units.en: He had parasols and command pennons set on the dike to show he would not stir.
units.literal: He ordered umbrella-fans and command banners brought and planted on the dike to show there would be no move.

units.zh: 叡素羸，每戰未嘗騎馬，以板輿自載，督厲衆軍。
units.en: Rui was slight of body; he never mounted in battle, riding a wooden litter while he harried the ranks.
units.literal: Rui had always been frail; in every battle he never rode a horse, but was carried in a wooden litter while he drove the army.

units.zh: 魏兵來鑿堤，叡親與爭之，魏軍少卻，因築壘於堤以自固。
units.en: Wei came to cut the dike; Rui fought them hand to hand, they gave ground, and he threw up ramparts on the bank.
units.literal: The Wei soldiers came to breach the dike; Rui struggled with them in person, the Wei host fell back a little, and he built ramparts on the dike to make himself secure.

units.zh: 叡起鬬艦，高與合肥城等，四面臨之。
units.en: He built fighting towers level with Hefei's walls and closed in on four sides.
units.literal: Rui raised tower-ships as high as the walls of Hefei and pressed the city on every side.

units.zh: 魏人計窮，相與悲哭。
units.en: Wei was spent; men wept in each other's arms.
units.literal: The Wei men were at their wits' end and wept together.

units.zh: 叡攻具旣成，堰水又滿，魏救兵無所用。
units.en: His engines were ready and the water stood high; Wei's rescuers were useless.
units.literal: When Rui's siege engines were ready and the dammed water stood full, Wei's relief could do nothing.

units.zh: 魏守將杜元倫登城督戰，中弩死，城遂潰。
units.en: Du Yuanlun commanded from the wall, took a bolt, and fell; the city broke.
units.literal: Wei's defender Du Yuanlun climbed the wall to direct the fight, was struck by a crossbow bolt, and died; the city collapsed at once.

units.zh: 俘獲萬餘級，牛馬萬數，絹滿十間屋，悉充軍賞。
units.en: Prisoners passed ten thousand; cattle and horses beyond count; silk filled ten chambers—everything went to the soldiers.
units.literal: Captives numbered more than ten thousand ranks; cattle and horses by the ten-thousands; silk filled ten rooms—all went to reward the army.

units.zh: 叡每晝接客旅，夜算軍書，三更起張燈達曙，撫循其衆，常如不及，故投募之士爭歸之。
units.en: By day he met guests; by night he tallied dispatches—up at the third watch, lamps to dawn, tending his men as if he could never finish, so volunteers fought to serve under him.
units.literal: By day Rui received travelers; by night he reckoned military papers—rising at the third watch with lamps burning until dawn, comforting and guiding his men as though he could never do enough, so that men who came to enlist contended to join him.

units.zh: 所至頓舍脩立，館宇籓籬牆壁，皆應準繩。
units.en: Every halt became a measured camp—quarters, palisades, and walls squared to the rule.
units.literal: Wherever he halted he set up camp in proper order; lodges, fences, and walls all met the standard.

units.zh: 合肥旣平，高祖詔衆軍進次東陵。
units.en: Hefei fell; Gaozu ordered the hosts forward to Dongling.
units.literal: When Hefei was pacified, Gaozu ordered the armies to advance and encamp at Dongling.

units.zh: 東陵去魏甓城二十里，將會戰，有詔班師。
units.en: Dongling stood twenty li from Wei's Brick City; as battle neared, orders came to withdraw.
units.literal: Dongling lay twenty li from Wei's Brick City; battle was about to join when an edict recalled the army.

units.zh: 去賊旣近，懼爲所躡，叡悉遣輜重居前，身乘小輿殿后，魏人服叡威名，望之不敢逼，全軍而還。
units.en: The foe was near; he sent wagons ahead and rode a small litter in the rear—Wei feared his name and would not close; the army came home whole.
units.literal: The enemy was close; fearing pursuit, Rui sent all the baggage train ahead while he himself rode in a small litter at the rear—the Wei men revered Rui's name and dared not press him; the whole army returned intact.

units.zh: 至是遷豫州於合肥。
units.en: Then the seat of Yuzhou was shifted to Hefei.
units.literal: At that time Yuzhou's seat was moved to Hefei.

units.zh: 五年，魏中山王元英寇北徐州，圍刺史昌義之於鐘離，衆號百萬，連城四十餘。
units.en: In year 5 Yuan Ying, prince of Zhongshan, struck North Xuzhou and penned Chang Yizhi at Zhongli—"a million" men, forty-odd camps chained together.
units.literal: In the fifth year Wei's Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying raided North Xuzhou and besieged Inspector Chang Yizhi at Zhongli; they claimed a million men and more than forty linked camps.

units.zh: 高祖遣征北將軍曹景宗，都督衆軍二十萬以拒之。
units.en: Gaozu sent Cao Jingzong, general who pacifies the north, with two hundred thousand to meet them.
units.literal: Gaozu sent Pacification-North General Cao Jingzong to command two hundred thousand men to resist.

units.zh: 次邵陽洲，築壘相守，高祖詔叡率豫州之衆會焉。
units.en: They held Shaoyang Isle behind fresh ramparts; Gaozu told Rui to bring Yuzhou's army to the rendezvous.
units.literal: They encamped at Shaoyang Isle and built ramparts to hold each other; Gaozu ordered Rui to bring the forces of Yuzhou and join them.

units.zh: 叡自合肥逕道由陰陵大澤行，值澗穀，輒飛橋以濟。
units.en: He left Hefei by the straight track through Yinling's great bogs, bridging every gully as he came.
units.literal: Rui came from Hefei by the direct road through the great marshes of Yinling; whenever he met ravines he threw flying bridges across.

units.zh: 師人畏魏軍盛，多勸叡緩行。
units.en: His men dreaded Wei's numbers and begged him to march slowly.
units.literal: The soldiers feared the Wei host's strength and many urged Rui to go slowly.

units.zh: 叡曰：「鐘離今鑿穴而處，負戶而汲，車馳卒奔，猶恐其後，而況緩乎！
units.en: Rui said, "At Zhongli they burrow in the earth and haul water on their shoulders; chariots fly and runners dash, and still they fear they are late—shall we crawl?
units.literal: Rui said, "At Zhongli they are digging holes to live in and carrying water on their backs; chariots race and runners sprint, and still they fear they come too late—how much less should we linger!

units.zh: 魏人已墮吾腹中，卿曹勿憂也。」
units.en: Wei is already in my gut—have no fear."
units.literal: The Wei men are already in my belly—do not fret."

units.zh: 旬日而至邵陽。
units.en: In ten days he was at Shaoyang.
units.literal: Within ten days he reached Shaoyang.

units.zh: 初，高祖敕景宗曰：「韋叡，卿之鄉望，宜善敬之。」
units.en: Gaozu had told Jingzong, "Wei Rui is the great man of your district—treat him with respect."
units.literal: Earlier Gaozu had charged Jingzong, "Wei Rui is the leading man of your native place—you must honor him well."

units.zh: 景宗見叡，禮甚謹。
units.en: Jingzong received him with deep courtesy.
units.literal: Jingzong received Rui with the utmost courtesy.

units.zh: 高祖聞之，曰：「二將和，師必濟矣。」
units.en: Gaozu heard and said, "Two generals in accord—the host will win."
units.literal: When Gaozu heard of it he said, "When two generals are in harmony, the army will surely succeed."

units.zh: 叡於景宗營前二十里，夜掘長塹，樹鹿角，截洲爲城，比曉而營立。
units.en: Twenty li short of Jingzong's lines he dug a trench by night, planted stakes, and walled off the isle—by dawn a camp stood.
units.literal: Twenty li before Jingzong's camp, Rui dug a long trench by night, set antlers, and cut the isle into a walled camp; by dawn the fort stood.

units.zh: 元英大驚，以杖擊地曰：「是何神也！」
units.en: Yuan Ying was thunderstruck and beat the earth with his staff: "What sorcery is this!"
units.literal: Yuan Ying was greatly alarmed and struck the ground with his staff, crying, "What spirit is this!

units.zh: 明旦，英自率衆來戰，叡乘素木輿，執白角如意麾軍，一日數合，英甚憚其強。
units.en: At first light Ying came in person; Rui sat in a plain wooden litter, white ruyi in hand, and fought several rounds in a day—Ying dreaded his power.
units.literal: At dawn Ying himself led the host to battle; Rui rode a plain wooden litter, white horn ruyi in hand to command the ranks, clashing several times in a day—Ying greatly feared his strength.

units.zh: 魏軍又夜來攻城，飛矢雨集，叡子黯請下城以避箭，叡不許。
units.en: Wei stormed the wall by night; arrows poured. His son An begged to come down; Rui refused.
units.literal: The Wei army came again by night to storm the wall; arrows fell like rain. Rui's son An asked to leave the wall to escape the shafts; Rui would not allow it.

units.zh: 軍中驚，叡於城上厲聲呵之，乃定。
units.en: The ranks wavered; he roared from the battlements and they steadied.
units.literal: Panic ran through the army; Rui shouted from the wall in a fierce voice and the host steadied.

units.zh: 魏人先於邵陽洲兩岸爲兩橋，樹柵數百步，跨淮通道。
units.en: Wei had bridged both shores of Shaoyang with palisades for hundreds of paces, a road across the Huai.
units.literal: The Wei men had earlier built twin bridges on both banks of Shaoyang Isle, with palisades for several hundred paces, spanning the Huai as a road.

units.zh: 叡裝大艦，使梁郡太守馮道根、廬江太守裴邃、秦郡太守李文釗等爲水軍。
units.en: He fitted great ships and set Feng Daogen of Liangjun, Pei Sui of Lujiang, and Li Wenzhao of Qinjun over the fleet.
units.literal: Rui fitted great warships and made Administrator of Liangjun Feng Daogen, Administrator of Lujiang Pei Sui, and Administrator of Qinjun Li Wenzhao command the river force.

units.zh: 值淮水暴長，叡卽遣之，鬬艦競發，皆臨敵壘。
units.en: The Huai swelled; he launched at once—tower-ships leaped forward and closed on the Wei lines.
units.literal: The Huai suddenly rose in flood; Rui sent the fleet at once, tower-ships racing out, all bearing on the enemy ramparts.

units.zh: 以小船載草，灌之以膏，從而焚其橋。
units.en: Small craft heaped greased grass and fired the bridges in their wake.
units.literal: Small boats carried grass soaked in grease and set the bridges ablaze behind them.

units.zh: 風怒火盛，煙塵晦冥，敢死之士，拔柵斫橋，水又漂疾，倏忽之間，橋柵盡壞。
units.en: Wind made a furnace of the sky; men who did not care for life wrenched down stakes and chopped bridges while the flood raced—bridges and palisades vanished in a breath.
units.literal: Wind fed the flames until smoke and dust blotted the sky; death-defying men tore down palisades and hacked the bridges, while the current ran fierce—in an instant bridges and stakes were gone.

units.zh: 而道根等皆身自搏戰，軍人奮勇，呼聲動天地，無不一當百，魏人大潰。
units.en: Feng Daogen and the others fought in the van; the soldiers roared till heaven shook, each man worth a hundred—Wei broke completely.
units.literal: Feng Daogen and the rest fought hand to hand themselves; the soldiers fought with fury, their cries shaking heaven and earth, none meeting less than a hundred—the Wei host collapsed utterly.

units.zh: 元英見橋絕，脫身遁去。
units.en: Yuan Ying saw the bridges destroyed and ran.
units.literal: Yuan Ying saw the bridges gone and fled for his life.

units.zh: 魏軍趨水死者十餘萬，斬首亦如之。
units.en: Men drowning in the river ran to the hundred-thousands; heads heaped as high.
units.literal: Wei soldiers rushing to the water drowned by the hundred-thousands; heads taken were as many.

units.zh: 其餘釋甲稽顙，乞爲囚奴，猶數十萬。
units.en: The rest dropped their armor and kowtowed, begging to become prisoners and slaves--still hundreds of thousands.
units.literal: The rest cast off armor and bowed their foreheads, begging to be prisoners—still several hundred thousand.

units.zh: 所獲軍實牛馬，不可勝紀。
units.en: Booty in arms, cattle, and horses passed counting.
units.literal: Arms, cattle, and horses captured could not be counted.

units.zh: 叡遣報昌義之，義之且悲且喜，不暇答語，但叫曰：「更生！
units.en: Rui sent to Chang Yizhi; Yizhi wept and laughed, unable to answer, and could only shout, "Born again!
units.literal: Rui sent word to Chang Yizhi; Yizhi was by turns grieving and glad, too overwhelmed to answer, and could only cry, "Reborn!

units.zh: 更生！」
units.en: Born again!"
units.literal: Reborn!"

units.zh: 高祖遣中書郎周捨勞於淮上，叡積所獲於軍門，捨觀之，謂叡曰：「君此獲復與熊耳山等。」
units.en: Gaozu sent Zhou She to comfort the Huai army; Rui heaped booty at the gate. She said, "This haul matches Bear-Ear Mountain."
units.literal: Gaozu sent Palace Secretary Zhou She to reward and comfort the army on the Huai; Rui piled the spoils at the camp gate for him to see. She looked and said to Rui, "Your capture here rivals Bear-Ear Mountain."

units.zh: 以功增封七百戶，進爵爲侯，徵通直散騎常侍、右衛將軍。
units.en: His fief grew by seven hundred households, he became a marquis, and was called to court as regular attendant of direct transmission and right guard general.
units.literal: For his merit his fief was increased by seven hundred households, he was advanced to marquis, and summoned as Regular Attendant of Direct Transmission and Right Guard General.

units.zh: 七年，遷左衛將軍，俄爲安西長史、南郡太守，秩中二千石。
units.en: In year 7 he became left guard general, then chief clerk of Anxi and administrator of Nanjun at two-thousand-dan rank.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was made Left Guard General, then soon Anxi Chief Clerk and Administrator of Nanjun at the salary of two thousand dan.

units.zh: 會司州刺史馬仙琕北伐還軍，爲魏人所躡，三關擾動，詔叡督衆軍援焉。
units.en: Ma Xianbi of Sizhou marched north and was chased home by Wei; the Three Passes trembled, and Rui was ordered to command the rescue.
units.literal: When Sizhou Inspector Ma Xianbi marched north and returned, Wei pursued him; the Three Passes were shaken, and an edict made Rui commander of the relief armies.

units.zh: 叡至安陸，增築城二丈餘，更開大塹，起高樓，衆頗譏其示弱。
units.en: At Anlu he raised walls two zhang higher, dug a deep moat, and built tall towers—many sneered that he showed weakness.
units.literal: Rui reached Anlu, raised the walls more than two zhang, opened a great trench, and built tall towers; many mocked him for showing fear.

units.zh: 叡曰：「不然，爲將當有怯時，不可專勇。」
units.en: Rui said, "No—a general must know fear; bravery alone will not do."
units.literal: Rui said, "Not so—a commander must know when to be timid; courage alone is not enough.

units.zh: 是時元英復追仙琕，將復邵陽之恥，聞叡至，乃退。
units.en: Yuan Ying chased Xianbi again to avenge Shaoyang; hearing Rui had arrived, he retreated.
units.literal: At that time Yuan Ying again pursued Xianbi, meaning to wash away the shame of Shaoyang; when he heard Rui had come, he withdrew.

units.zh: 帝亦詔罷軍。
units.en: The throne recalled the host.
units.literal: The emperor also ordered the armies disbanded.

units.zh: 明年，遷信武將軍、江州刺史。
units.en: Next year he became trustworthy-war general and inspector of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: The next year he was made Trustworthy-War General and Inspector of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 九年，徵員外散騎常侍、右衛將軍，累遷左衛將軍、太子詹事，尋加通直散騎常侍。
units.en: In year 9 he was recalled as supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and right guard general, then advanced through left guard general and supervisor of the crown prince's household, with the added title regular attendant of direct transmission.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned as Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Right Guard General, and rose repeatedly to Left Guard General and Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household, then with the additional title Regular Attendant of Direct Transmission.

units.zh: 十三年，遷智武將軍、丹陽尹，以公事免。
units.en: In year 13 he was made Intelligent Martial General and intendant of Danyang, then dismissed on public business.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Intelligent Martial General and Intendant of Danyang, then removed from office on public business.

units.zh: 頃之，起爲中護軍。
units.en: Soon he was recalled as Central Protector General.
units.literal: Before long he was recalled as Central Protector General.

units.zh: 十四年，出爲平北將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
units.en: In year 14 he went out as General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and inspector of Yongzhou.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year he went out as General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and Inspector of Yongzhou.

units.zh: 初，叡起兵鄉中，客陰儁光泣止叡，叡還爲州，儁光道候叡，叡笑謂之曰：「若從公言，乞食於路矣。」
units.en: When Rui first raised troops at home, his guest Yin Junguang wept and tried to stop him; on returning as inspector, Junguang met him on the road, and Rui laughed and said, "Had I taken your advice, I would be begging along the highway."
units.literal: Earlier, when Rui had raised troops in his home district, his guest Yin Junguang wept and tried to stop him; when Rui returned as inspector, Junguang met him on the road, and Rui laughed and said to him, "Had I followed your advice, I would be begging food on the highway."

units.zh: 餉耕牛十頭。
units.en: He gave him ten draft oxen.
units.literal: He presented ten draft oxen.

units.zh: 叡於故舊，無所遺惜，士大夫年七十以上，多與假板縣令，鄉里甚懷之。
units.en: Toward old friends Rui was unstinting; for gentry over seventy he often gave acting county magistrate posts, and the district loved him for it.
units.literal: Toward old friends Rui held nothing back; for scholar-officials over seventy he often granted acting county magistrate appointments, and the district thought warmly of him.

units.zh: 十五年，拜表致仕，優詔不許。
units.en: In year 15 he petitioned to retire; a gracious edict refused.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year he memorialized to retire; a gracious edict refused.

units.zh: 十七年，徵散騎常侍、護軍將軍，尋給鼓吹一部，入直殿省。
units.en: In year 17 he was summoned as Regular Attendant and Protector of the Army; soon he received martial pipes and drums and took regular duty in the Hall Department.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he was summoned as Regular Attendant and Protector of the Army General; soon he was given one set of martial pipes and drums and entered regular duty in the Hall Department.

units.zh: 居朝廷，恂恂未嘗忤視，高祖甚禮敬之。
units.en: At court he was deferential and never met others' eyes; Gaozu treated him with great respect.
units.literal: In court he was respectful and never met others' eyes directly; Gaozu greatly honored him.

units.zh: 性慈愛，撫孤兄子過於己子，歷官所得祿賜，皆散之親故，家無餘財。
units.en: Kind by nature, he raised his orphaned nephews more devotedly than his own sons and gave every salary and gift to kin and friends, leaving nothing at home.
units.literal: By nature he was kindly; he raised his orphaned elder brother's sons more devotedly than his own, and whatever salary and gifts his offices brought he gave away to kin and friends, leaving nothing at home.

units.zh: 後爲護軍，居家無事，慕萬石、陸賈之爲人，因畫之於壁以自玩。
units.en: Later, idle at home as Protector of the Army, he admired the Wan Shi and Lu Jia and painted them on his wall for amusement.
units.literal: Later, as Protector of the Army with nothing to do at home, he admired the conduct of the Wan Shi clan and Lu Jia and painted them on his wall for his own pleasure.

units.zh: 時雖老，暇日猶課諸兒以學。
units.en: Though old, on free days he still drilled his sons in learning.
units.literal: Though old, on free days he still set lessons for his sons.

units.zh: 第三子稜，尤明經史，世稱其洽聞，叡每坐棱使說書，其所發擿，稜猶弗之逮也。
units.en: His third son Ling knew the classics and histories especially well and was called broadly learned. Rui always seated Ling and had him lecture on books; the points Rui raised, Ling still could not match.
units.literal: His third son Ling was especially versed in the classics and histories; the age called him broadly learned. Rui would seat Ling and have him explain the books; the points Rui raised, Ling still could not match.

units.zh: 高祖方銳意釋氏，天下咸從風而化；
units.en: Gaozu was then intent on Buddhism, and the realm followed;
units.literal: Gaozu was then keen on Buddhism, and all under heaven followed the fashion;

units.zh: 叡自以信受素薄，位居大臣，不欲與俗俯仰，所行略如他日。
units.en: Rui felt his faith had always been thin; as a great minister he would not bob with fashion, and lived much as before.
units.literal: Rui felt his own faith had always been thin; holding a minister's rank, he did not wish to bob with the crowd, and his conduct stayed much as before.

units.zh: 普通元年夏，遷侍中、車騎將軍，以疾未拜。
units.en: In summer of Putong year 1 he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry but did not take office because of illness.
units.literal: In the summer of the first year of Putong he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry, but because of illness did not accept the appointment.

units.zh: 八月，卒于家，時年七十九。
units.en: In the eighth month he died at home at seventy-nine.
units.literal: In the eighth month he died at home, aged seventy-nine.

units.zh: 遺令薄葬，斂以時服。
units.en: He ordered a plain burial in seasonal dress.
units.literal: His final instructions ordered a plain burial, enshrouded in seasonal dress.

units.zh: 高祖卽日臨哭甚慟。
units.en: Gaozu came to mourn that same day and wept bitterly.
units.literal: Gaozu came that same day to mourn and wept bitterly.

units.zh: 賜錢十萬，布二百匹，東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，喪事取給於官，遣中書舍人監護。
units.en: He received a hundred thousand cash, two hundred bolts of cloth, eastern-garden funeral vessels, one court robe and one suit of clothes; the offices supplied the funeral, and a Secretariat Gentleman oversaw it.
units.literal: He was granted a hundred thousand cash, two hundred bolts of cloth, eastern-garden funeral vessels, one court robe, one suit of clothes; whatever the funeral required was to be supplied by the offices, and a Secretariat Gentleman was sent to oversee it.

units.zh: 贈侍中、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。
units.en: Posthumously he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Acting Three Excellencies with Opening Office.
units.literal: Posthumously he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Acting Three Excellencies with Opening Office.

units.zh: 諡曰嚴。
units.en: Posthumous title: Yan.
units.literal: Posthumous title: Yan.

units.zh: 初，邵陽之役，昌義之甚德叡，請曹景宗與叡會，因設錢二十萬官賭之，景宗擲得雉，叡徐擲得盧，遽取一子反之，曰「異事」，遂作塞。
units.en: At Shaoyang, Chang Yizhi was deeply grateful to Rui and asked Cao Jingzong to meet him; they wagered two hundred thousand cash. Jingzong threw pheasant; Rui slowly threw black, flipped one piece, said "Strange!" and forced a tie.
units.literal: Earlier, at the battle of Shaoyang, Chang Yizhi owed Rui a great debt and asked Cao Jingzong to meet with Rui; they set an official wager of two hundred thousand cash. Jingzong cast and got pheasant; Rui slowly cast and got black, then quickly took one piece and flipped it, saying "Strange!" and made a full tie.

units.zh: 景宗時與羣帥爭先啟之捷，叡獨居後，其不尚勝，率多如是，世尤以此賢之。
units.en: Jingzong often raced other commanders to report victory first; Rui alone held back. He seldom cared to win, and the age prized him for it.
units.literal: Jingzong often vied with the other commanders to be first in reporting victory; Rui alone held back. His disdain for winning was mostly like this, and the age especially praised him for it.

units.zh: 子放、正、稜、黯，放別有傳。
units.en: His sons Fang, Zheng, Ling, and An; Fang has a separate biography.
units.literal: His sons Fang, Zheng, Ling, and An—Fang has a separate biography.

units.zh: 正字敬直，起家南康王行參軍，稍遷中書侍郎，出爲襄陽太守。
units.en: Zheng, styled Jingzhi, began on the Prince of Nankang's staff, rose to Secretariat Gentleman, and went out as administrator of Xiangyang.
units.literal: Zheng, styled Jingzhi, began his career as an aide on the staff of the Prince of Nankang, was gradually promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, and went out as Administrator of Xiangyang.

units.zh: 初，正與東海王僧孺友善，及僧孺爲尚書吏部郎，參掌大選，賓友故人莫不傾意，正獨澹然。
units.en: Zheng had been close to Wang Sengru of Donghai; when Sengru became Director of Personnel and ran the great selection, friends all courted him—Zheng alone stayed aloof.
units.literal: Earlier Zheng had been friendly with Wang Sengru of Donghai; when Sengru became Director of Personnel in the Masters of Writing and took part in the great selection, friends and guests all leaned on him—Zheng alone stayed aloof.

units.zh: 及僧孺擯廢之後，正復篤素分，有逾曩日，論者稱焉。
units.en: After Sengru fell, Zheng kept their old bond warmer than before, and men praised him.
units.literal: After Sengru was cast out, Zheng again kept their old bond more warmly than in former days, and commentators praised him.

units.zh: 歷官至給事黃門侍郎。
units.en: He rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate.
units.literal: He rose in office to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate.

units.zh: 稜字威直，性恬素，以書史爲業，博物強記，當世之士，咸就質疑。
units.en: Ling, styled Weizhi, was quiet and plain, lived in books and histories, was broadly learned with a strong memory, and men of the age came to him with questions.
units.literal: Ling, styled Weizhi, was by nature quiet and plain; he made books and histories his profession, was broadly learned with a strong memory, and men of the age all came to him with questions.

units.zh: 起家安成王府行參軍，稍遷治書侍御史，太子僕，光祿卿。
units.en: He began on the Prince of Ancheng's staff, rose to Imperial Censor, Heir Apparent's Household Steward, and Director of the Bright Halls.
units.literal: He began his career as an aide on the staff of the Prince of Ancheng, was gradually promoted to Imperial Censor, Household Steward of the Heir Apparent, and Director of the Bright Halls.

units.zh: 著《漢書續訓》三卷。
units.en: He wrote Continued Lessons on the Han in three scrolls.
units.literal: He wrote Continued Lessons on the Han in three scrolls.

units.zh: 黯字務直，性強正，少習經史，有文詞。
units.en: An, styled Wuzhi, was forceful and upright; in youth he studied the classics and histories and wrote well.
units.literal: An, styled Wuzhi, was by nature forceful and upright; in youth he studied the classics and histories and had literary skill.

units.zh: 起家太子舍人，稍遷太僕卿，南豫州刺史，太府卿。
units.en: He began as Heir Apparent's Household Attendant, rose to Minister of the Imperial Studs, inspector of South Yuzhou, and Minister of the Grand Storehouse.
units.literal: He began his career as Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent, was gradually promoted to Minister of the Imperial Studs, Inspector of South Yuzhou, and Minister of the Grand Storehouse.

units.zh: 侯景濟江，黯屯六門，尋改爲都督城西面諸軍事。
units.en: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, An held the Six Gates; soon he was made commander of the western defenses.
units.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, An garrisoned the Six Gates; soon he was made commander of all military affairs on the city's western face.

units.zh: 時景於城外起東西二土山，城內亦作以應之，太宗親自負土，哀太子以下躬執畚鍤。
units.en: Jing built east and west earthen mounds outside the wall and matching mounds within; Taizong personally carried earth, and the Lamenting Heir Apparent and those below him carried earth with shovel and basket.
units.literal: At that time Jing raised east and west earthen mounds outside the wall, and within the city others were built to match; Taizong personally carried earth, and the Lamenting Heir Apparent and those below him personally took shovel and basket in hand.

units.zh: 黯守西土山，晝夜苦戰，以功授輕車將軍，加持節。
units.en: An held the western mound and fought day and night; for merit he was made General of Light Chariots with staff of authority.
units.literal: An held the western mound, fighting bitterly day and night; for merit he was made General of Light Chariots with added staff of authority.

units.zh: 卒於城內，贈散騎常侍、左衛將軍。
units.en: He died in the city and was posthumously made Regular Attendant and Left Guard General.
units.literal: He died within the city and was posthumously made Regular Attendant and Left Guard General.

units.zh: 叡族弟愛。
units.en: Rui's cousin Ai.
units.literal: Rui's cousin by the clan Ai.

units.zh: 愛字孝友，沈靜有器局。
units.en: Ai, styled Xiaoyou, was calm and had real capacity.
units.literal: Ai, styled Xiaoyou, was calm and possessed capacity.

units.zh: 高祖父廣，晉後軍將軍、北平太守。
units.en: His great-great-grandfather Guang was Jin Rear Army General and administrator of Beiping.
units.literal: His great-great-grandfather Guang was Jin Rear Army General and Administrator of Beiping.

units.zh: 曾祖軌，以孝武太元之初，南遷襄陽，爲本州別駕，散騎侍郎。
units.en: His great-grandfather Gui, at the start of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era, moved south to Xiangyang, became the province's Separate Cart, then Regular Attendant.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Gui, at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era, moved south to Xiangyang and became the province's Separate Cart, then Regular Attendant.

units.zh: 祖公循，宋義陽太守。
units.en: His grandfather Gongxun was Song administrator of Yiyang.
units.literal: His grandfather on the father's side Gongxun was Song Administrator of Yiyang.

units.zh: 父義正，早卒。
units.en: His father Yizheng died young.
units.literal: His father Yizheng died young.

units.zh: 愛少而偏孤，事母以孝聞。
units.en: Ai lost his father early and was known for filial service to his mother.
units.literal: Ai lost his father early and served his mother with a fame for filial piety.

units.zh: 性清介，不妄交遊，而篤志好學，每虛室獨坐，遊心墳素，而埃塵滿席，寂若無人。
units.en: Pure and aloof, he made friends carefully yet loved learning; he often sat alone with his mind in the classics, dust on the mat, silent as if alone.
units.literal: By nature he was pure and aloof, not making friends rashly, yet he set his will on learning; he often sat alone in an empty room with his mind in the classics, dust on the mat, silent as if no one were there.

units.zh: 年十二，嘗游京師，值天子出遊南苑，邑裏喧嘩，老幼爭觀，愛獨端坐讀書，手不釋卷，宗族見者，莫不異焉。
units.en: At twelve he was in the capital when the Son of Heaven went to the Southern Park; the streets roared as old and young competed to watch. Ai alone sat upright reading and never put down his scroll, and all his kinsmen who saw him marveled at him.
units.literal: At twelve he once traveled to the capital; when the Son of Heaven went out to the Southern Park the streets were noisy, old and young scrambling to watch—Ai alone sat reading and never put down his scroll; kin who saw it all marveled.

units.zh: 及長，博學有文才，尤善《周易》及《春秋左氏》義。
units.en: Grown, he was broadly learned and literary, especially skilled in the Changes and the Zuo Tradition to the Annals.
units.literal: When grown he was broadly learned and had literary talent, especially skilled in the meaning of the Changes and the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

units.zh: 袁顗爲雍州刺史，辟爲主簿。
units.en: Yuan Hao, inspector of Yongzhou, recruited him as chief clerk.
units.literal: Yuan Hao was Inspector of Yongzhou and recruited him as chief clerk.

units.zh: 遭母憂，廬於墓側，負土起墳。
units.en: At his mother's death he built a hut by the tomb and carried earth for the mound.
units.literal: When his mother died he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to raise the mound.

units.zh: 高祖臨雍州，聞之，親往臨弔。
units.en: When Gaozu held Yongzhou he heard and came in person to mourn.
units.literal: When Gaozu held Yongzhou he heard of it and came in person to mourn at the site.

units.zh: 服闋，引爲中兵參軍。
units.en: When mourning ended he was made Central Army Aide.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was brought in as Central Army Aide.

units.zh: 義師之起也，以愛爲壯武將軍、冠軍南平王司馬，帶襄陽令。
units.en: When the righteous army rose, Ai was made Valiant Martial General and major to the Prince of Nanping, Champion, with concurrent charge as magistrate of Xiangyang.
units.literal: When the righteous army rose, Ai was made Valiant Martial General and Major to the Prince of Nanping, Champion, with concurrent charge as Magistrate of Xiangyang.

units.zh: 時京邑未定，雍州空虛，魏興太守顏僧都等據郡反，州內驚擾，百姓攜貳。
units.en: The capital was unsettled and Yongzhou empty; Wei Xing administrator Yan Sangdu and others held the commandery in revolt, and the province shook.
units.literal: At that time the capital was not yet settled and Yongzhou was empty; Wei Xing Administrator Yan Sangdu and others held the commandery in revolt; within the province there was alarm and the people wavered.

units.zh: 愛沉敏有謀，素爲州里信伏，乃推心撫御，曉示逆順；
units.en: Ai was deep, keen, and trusted in the district; he won hearts with open care and showed who was loyal and who rebel;
units.literal: Ai was deep, keen, and resourceful and had long been trusted by the district; he won hearts with open-handed care and made clear who was rebel and who loyal;

units.zh: 兼率募鄉里，得千餘人，與僧都等戰於始平郡南，大破之，百姓乃安。
units.en: he also recruited more than a thousand men locally and routed Sangdu south of Shiping commandery; the people were at peace.
units.literal: he also led recruitment in the home district and got more than a thousand men; with Sangdu and the rest he fought south of Shiping commandery, routed them utterly, and the people were then at peace.

units.zh: 蕭穎胄之死也，和帝徵兵襄陽，愛從始興王憺赴焉。
units.en: When Xiao Yingchen died, Emperor He summoned troops at Xiangyang; Ai followed Prince of Shixing Dan.
units.literal: When Xiao Yingchen died, Emperor He summoned troops at Xiangyang; Ai followed the Prince of Shixing Dan to answer.

units.zh: 先是，巴東太守蕭璝、巴東太守魯休烈舉兵來逼荊州，及憺至，令愛書諭之，璝卽日請降。
units.en: Earlier Eastern Ba administrators Xiao Huang and Lu Xiulie had raised troops against Jingzhou; when Dan came he had Ai write to them, and Huang surrendered the same day.
units.literal: Earlier, Eastern Ba Administrator Xiao Huang and Eastern Ba Administrator Lu Xiulie had raised troops to press Jingzhou; when Dan arrived he had Ai write to instruct them, and Huang that same day asked to surrender.

units.zh: 中興二年，從和帝東下。
units.en: In Zhongxing year 2 he followed Emperor He east.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he followed Emperor He east.

units.zh: 高祖受禪，進號輔國將軍，仍爲驍騎將軍，尋除寧蜀太守，與益州刺史鄧元起西上襲劉季連，行至公安，道病卒，贈衛尉卿。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Ai was advanced to General Who Assists the State, then kept as General of Valiant Cavalry, made administrator of Ning Shu, and with Yizhou inspector Deng Yuanqi went west against Liu Jilian; at Gong'an he died on the road and was posthumously made Minister of the Guard.
units.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Ai's rank was advanced to General Who Assists the State; he remained General of Valiant Cavalry, was soon made Administrator of Ning Shu, and with Yizhou Inspector Deng Yuanqi went west to attack Liu Jilian; on reaching Gong'an he died of illness on the road and was posthumously made Minister of the Guard.

units.zh: 子乾向，官至驍騎將軍，征北長史，汝陰、鐘離二郡太守。
units.en: His son Ganxiang rose to General of Valiant Cavalry, chief clerk on the northern expedition, and administrator of Ruyin and Zhongli.
units.literal: His son Ganxiang rose in office to General of Valiant Cavalry, Chief Clerk of the Army on the Northern Expedition, and Administrator of the two commanderies of Ruyin and Zhongli.

units.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：昔竇融以河右歸漢，終爲盛族；
units.en: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Dou Rong once submitted Hexi to Han and became a great clan;
units.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: In old times Dou Rong submitted the lands west of the Yellow River to Han and in the end became a great clan;

units.zh: 柳惔舉南鄭響從，而家聲弗霣，時哉！
units.en: Liu Tan raised Nan Zheng in response and followed, yet his family name did not sink—the times favored it!
units.literal: Liu Tan raised Nan Zheng in response and followed, yet his family's renown did not sink—the times were right!

units.zh: 忱之謀畫，亦用有成，智矣。
units.en: Liu Chen's plans too succeeded—how wise!
units.literal: Liu Chen's planning too had its successes—how wise!

units.zh: 韋叡起上庸以附義，其地比惔則薄，及合肥、邵陽之役，其功甚盛，推而弗有，君子哉！
units.en: Wei Rui rose from Shangyong for the righteous cause; his base was poorer than Tan's, yet at Hefei and Shaoyang his merit was great, and he yielded without claiming it—a gentleman indeed!
units.literal: Wei Rui rose from Shangyong to join the righteous cause; his territory was poorer than Tan's, yet at Hefei and Shaoyang his merit was very great, and he yielded without claiming it—a gentleman indeed!

units.zh: 賾與河南元善、河東柳䛒、太原王劭、吳興姚察、琅琊諸葛潁、信都劉焯、河間劉炫相善，每因休假，清談竟日。
units.en: Ze was on good terms with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bi of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on holidays they would converse in pure talk all day.
units.literal: Ze was on good terms with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bi of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on holidays they would converse in pure talk all day.

units.zh: 隨道恭至義陽，會中山王英平義陽，獲焉。
units.en: He followed Daogong to Yiyang, and when Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying pacified Yiyang he was taken captive.
units.literal: He followed Daogong to Yiyang; when Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying pacified Yiyang he was taken captive.

units.zh: 英亡，亮奔赴，盡其哀慟。
units.en: When Yuan Ying died, Liang rushed to the funeral and mourned with the deepest grief.
units.literal: When Yuan Ying died Liang rushed to the funeral and mourned with the utmost grief.

units.zh: 英素聞其名，以禮待接。
units.en: Yuan Ying had long heard his name and received him with courtesy.
units.literal: Yuan Ying had long heard his name and received him with courtesy.

units.zh: 亮性清靜，後隱居嵩山，感英之德，以時展覲。
units.en: Liang's nature was pure and quiet; later he withdrew to Mount Song, moved by Yuan Ying's virtue, and from time to time paid him respectful visits.
units.literal: Liang's nature was pure and quiet; later he secluded himself on Mount Song, moved by Yuan Ying's virtue, and from time to time paid respectful visits.

units.zh: 永明八年，荊州刺史巴東王子響稱兵反，旣敗，焚燒府舍，官曹文書，一時蕩盡。
units.en: In Yongming year eight Prince Zixiang of Badong rebelled; defeated, he burned the offices and every record was lost.
units.literal: In Yongming year eight the Prince of Badong Zixiang raised troops in rebellion; when he was defeated he burned the government offices and every document in the bureaus was lost at once.

units.zh: 高祖以西臺將鄧元起爲益州刺史。
units.en: Gaozu made western headquarters general Deng Yuanqi Yizhou inspector.
units.literal: Gaozu made western headquarters general Deng Yuanqi inspector of Yizhou.

units.zh: 元起，南郡人。
units.en: Yuanqi came from Nanjun commandery.
units.literal: Yuanqi was a man of Nanjun commandery.

units.zh: 天監元年六月，元起至巴西，季連遣其將李奉伯等拒戰。
units.en: In the sixth month of Tianjian year one Yuanqi reached Baxi; Lijian sent Li Fengbo and others to fight.
units.literal: In the sixth month of Tianjian year one Yuanqi reached Baxi; Lijian sent his generals Li Fengbo and others to fight.

units.zh: 元起稍進圍之。
units.en: Yuanqi slowly advanced and besieged him.
units.literal: Yuanqi slowly advanced and besieged him.

units.zh: 元起誅李奉伯幷諸渠帥，送季連還京師。
units.en: Yuanqi executed Li Fengbo and the other ringleaders and sent Lijian back to the capital.
units.literal: Yuanqi executed Li Fengbo and the other ringleaders and sent Lijian back to the capital.

units.zh: 季連爲南郡之時，素薄元起。
units.en: When Lijian had held Nanjun he had always looked down on Yuanqi.
units.literal: When Lijian had held Nanjun he had always looked down on Yuanqi.

units.zh: 至是說元起曰：「益州亂離已久，公私府庫必多秏失，劉益州臨歸空竭，豈辦復能遠遣候遞。
units.en: Now he told Yuanqi, "Yizhou has been torn apart for years; public and private treasuries must be drained. When Inspector Liu leaves he will empty everything—how could he still send escorts from afar?
units.literal: Now he told Yuanqi: "Yizhou has been in disorder long; public and private treasuries must be drained. When Inspector Liu leaves he will empty everything—how could he still send escorts far away?

units.zh: 元起許之。
units.en: Yuanqi agreed.
units.literal: Yuanqi agreed.

units.zh: 於是軍府大懼，謂元起至必誅季連，禍及黨與，競言之於季連。
units.en: The military prefecture was terrified, saying when Yuanqi came he would punish Lijian and drag down everyone linked with him; they rushed to tell Lijian.
units.literal: The military prefecture was terrified, saying when Yuanqi came he would surely punish Lijian and bring disaster on all linked with him; they rushed to tell Lijian.

units.zh: 又惡昔之不禮元起也，益憤懣。
units.en: and he hated his old rudeness to Yuanqi, which deepened his rage.
units.literal: and he hated his old rudeness to Yuanqi, which deepened his rage.

units.zh: 使歸，元起收兵于巴西以待之，季連誅士略三子。
units.en: When the messengers returned, Yuanqi gathered troops in Baxi to wait; Lijian executed Shilve's three sons.
units.literal: When the messengers returned, Yuanqi gathered troops in Baxi to wait; Lijian executed Shilve's three sons.

units.zh: 元起遷季連於城外，俄而造焉，待之以禮。
units.en: Yuanqi moved Lijian outside the walls and soon came to visit, treating him with courtesy.
units.literal: Yuanqi moved Lijian outside the walls and soon came to visit, treating him with courtesy.

units.zh: 初，元起在道，懼事不集，無以爲賞，士之至者，皆許以辟命，於是受別駕、治中檄者，將二千人。
units.en: Earlier, on the road Yuanqi had feared failure and lacked rewards; to every officer who came he promised a commission—thus nearly two thousand held writs as deputy inspector or chief administrator.
units.literal: Earlier, while Yuanqi was on the road he had feared failure and lacked rewards; to every officer who came he promised a commission—thus nearly two thousand held writs as deputy inspector or chief administrator.

units.zh: 叡遣所督將馮道根、李文釗、裴邃、韋寂等乘艦登岸，擊魏洲上軍盡殪。
units.en: Rui sent Feng Daogen, Li Wenzhao, Pei Sui, Wei Ji, and other generals under his command to land from the ships and slaughter the Wei troops on the isle.
units.literal: Rui sent the generals under his command—Feng Daogen, Li Wenzhao, Pei Sui, Wei Ji, and others—to board the warships, land, and annihilate the Wei troops on the isle.

units.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：王珍國、申胄、徐元瑜、李居士，齊末咸爲列將，擁強兵，或面縛請罪，或斬關獻捷；
units.en: Chen minister of personnel Yao Cha said: Wang Zhenguo, Shen Gou, Xu Yuanyu, and Li Jushi—at the end of Qi all were ranked generals with strong armies; some bound themselves and pleaded guilt, some cut the passes and offered victory;
units.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Wang Zhenguo, Shen Gou, Xu Yuanyu, and Li Jushi—at the end of Qi all were ranked generals holding strong armies; some bound themselves and begged mercy, some cut the passes and presented victory;

units.zh: 胄、元瑜、居士入梁事迹鮮，故不爲之傳。
units.en: Gou, Yuanyu, and Jushi left little record after entering Liang, so no biographies were written for them.
units.literal: Gou, Yuanyu, and Jushi had few deeds recorded after entering Liang, so biographies were not written for them.

units.zh: 王珍國 馬仙琕 張齊
units.en: Wang Zhenguo; Ma Xianpin; Zhang Qi
units.literal: Wang Zhenguo; Ma Xianpin; Zhang Qi

units.zh: 馬仙琕，字靈馥，扶風郿人也。
units.en: Ma Xianpin, styled Lingfu, came from Mei in Fufeng.
units.literal: Ma Xianpin, styled Lingfu, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.

units.zh: 初，仙琕幼名仙婢，及長，以「婢」名不典，乃以「玉」代「女」，因成「琕」云。
units.en: At first Xianpin's childhood name was Xianbi; when grown, because "bi" as a name was not proper, he replaced the female radical with jade and made "Xianpin," it is said.
units.literal: At first Xianpin's childhood name was Xianbi; when grown, because "bi" as a name was not proper, he replaced "woman" with "jade," thus making "Xianpin," it is said.

units.zh: 諡曰剛。
units.en: Posthumous title: Gang.
units.literal: Posthumous title: Gang.

units.zh: 以功封浛洭縣伯，邑四百戶，仍遷都督司州諸軍事、司州刺史，輔國將軍如故。
units.en: For merit he was enfeoffed baron of Hansui with four hundred households, then commander of Si military affairs and Si inspector, supporting-the-state general as before.
units.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Hansui with four hundred households, and was then transferred to commander of Si military affairs and Si inspector, supporting-the-state general as before.

units.zh: 永元中，蕭遙光、崔慧景亂，累有戰功，以勳至前將軍。
units.en: In Yongyuan, Xiao Yaoguang and Cui Huijing rebelled; he won repeated battle merit and rose to front general.
